related_questions.question: Why could reducing the rate of cell division be helpful in treating cancer?
related_questions.snippet: The ability of chemotherapy to kill cancer cells depends on its ability to halt cell division. Usually, cancer drugs work by damaging the RNA or DNA that tells the cell how to copy itself in division. If the cancer cells are unable to divide, they die.
related_questions.title: Cancer Cells and Chemotherapy - Chemocare

related_questions.question: Why does chemotherapy reduce white blood cells?
related_questions.snippet: Certain chemotherapy drugs can damage your bone marrow — the spongy material found in your bones. Your bone marrow makes blood cells, which grow rapidly, making them very sensitive to the effects of chemotherapy. Chemotherapy kills many of the cells in your bone marrow, but the cells recover with time.

related_questions.question: What is the use of drugs to treat cancer by destroying or slowing the growth of cancer cells?
related_questions.snippet: Chemotherapy works against cancer by killing fast-growing cancer cells. Chemotherapy (also called chemo) is a type of cancer treatment that uses drugs to kill cancer cells.

related_questions.question: Does cancer cause low white blood cell count?

text_blocks.snippet: Yes, cancer and cancer treatments can cause a low white blood cell count, also known as leukopenia or neutropenia. This occurs because cancer can directly affect the bone marrow, where white blood cells are produced, or because treatments like chemotherapy can damage these cells.
snippet_highlighted_words: Yes, cancer and cancer treatments can cause a low white blood cell count

list.title: Cancer's Impact on Bone Marrow:
list.snippet: Certain cancers, especially those that affect the bone marrow like leukemia, can disrupt the production of healthy white blood cells.

list.title: Cancer Treatments:
list.snippet: Chemotherapy and radiation therapy, common cancer treatments, can damage bone marrow cells, including those that produce white blood cells, leading to a decrease in their numbers.

list.title: Increased Infection Risk:
list.snippet: White blood cells, particularly neutrophils, are crucial for fighting off infections. A low white blood cell count makes individuals more susceptible to infections.

list.title: Monitoring Blood Counts:
list.snippet: Doctors closely monitor white blood cell counts during cancer treatment to assess the impact of therapy and to take precautions to prevent or manage infections.

list.title: Specific White Blood Cell Types:
list.snippet: Different types of white blood cells, like neutrophils, lymphocytes, and monocytes, have different roles in immunity. Cancer and its treatments can affect these cell types in various ways.

list.title: Other Causes:
list.snippet: While cancer and its treatments are common causes of low white blood cell counts, other factors like infections, certain medications, and autoimmune conditions can also contribute.
